@.syntax:
@ row, col [SAY expr [PICTURE mask$]] [GET target [PICTURE mask$] [REQUIRED] [VALID condition] [MESSAGE text$] [HINT text$] [WHEN condition] [LOOKUP (SELECT ...)]]
@ row, col BUTTON label$ [CANCEL]
GET ... CHECKBOX | GET ... LIST "a,b,c" | GET ... LIST (SELECT ...)
@.desc: SAY writes text at a position (PICTURE formats it as FORMAT$ does). GET adds an entry field after the SAY text for a variable, a hash field (rec.name) or an array element (a(2)); READ edits the fields. GET pictures: @! upper case, @L lower case, @Sn width n, or a template where 9 = digit, A = letter, N = letter or digit, X = any, ! = upper case, and other characters are fixed; a template field must be left empty or filled in completely. REQUIRED fields (marked *) must be filled in before the form is saved. VALID is checked when the field is left going forward (going back is never refused); MESSAGE text is shown on the bottom line when it fails. Saving the form (a button, PgDn, Ctrl-W, Enter on the last field) checks every field's REQUIRED and VALID, visited or not, and goes to the first that fails. HINT text is shown on the bottom line while the cursor is in the field. WHEN skips the field when false. LOOKUP gives a list of allowed values (first column): F2 opens it, and leaving with a value not in the list opens it too.
examples: @ 7, 10 SAY "State: " GET state$ PICTURE "!!" LOOKUP (SELECT code, name FROM states)
@ 8, 10 SAY "Credit: " GET credit VALID credit <= 5000 MESSAGE "Limit is 5,000" WHEN type$ = "B"
@ 9, 10 SAY "Phone: " GET phone$ PICTURE "@R (999) 999-9999" HINT "Ten digits"

ALERT.syntax: choice = ALERT(message$ [, button1$, button2$, ...] | ALERT(message$, buttons_array)
ALERT.desc: Shows a centred message box with buttons and puts the screen back afterwards. ';' in the message starts a new line. Left/Right move, Enter chooses, a button's first letter chooses it. Returns the button number from 1, or 0 for Esc. With no buttons there is one OK button.
examples: IF ALERT("Delete this customer?", "No", "Yes") = 2 THEN DELETE FROM customers WHERE id = :id;

ANALYZE.desc: Scans a file and reports statistics/structure. Type HELP ANALYZE CSV for specifics.

ANALYZE CSV.desc: Analyzes CSV structure, column types, and validity.

ANALYZE FIXED.desc: Analyzes fixed-width files. If FIELDS is omitted, it attempts to auto-detect columns.

ANALYZE JSON.desc: Scans a JSON file, or every file matching a wildcard, to determine key consistency. SAVE SCHEMA TO writes the merged structure for UPGRADE JSON.

ANALYZE TEXT.desc: Reports file statistics: encoding, line endings (CRLF/LF), line counts, and size.

ANALYZE XML.desc: Scans XML structure/namespaces. Use SAVE SCHEMA to generate a mapping for UPGRADE XML.

ARRAY.desc: Creates a new array initialized with the given values.

BELL.desc: Plays a system sound (beep) to alert the user.

BOX.syntax: BOX top, left, bottom, right [, title$] [DOUBLE] [SHADOW]
BOX.desc: Draws a box with line characters and clears its inside in the current COLOR. The title is centred in the top line. SHADOW darkens the two columns to its right and the row below. Pop-ups (MENU, ALERT, pull-downs, pickers, EDIT RECORD, PROGRESS) have shadows unless SET SHADOW OFF.

BROWSE.syntax: BROWSE (SELECT ...) | BROWSE table$ [EDIT [KEY key$] [WHEN condition [MESSAGE text$]]] [AT top, left, bottom, right] [TITLE t$] [FREEZE n] [FORMAT col mask$, ...] [COLOR col$] [EXIT ON keys$] [INTO var] [DETAIL (SELECT ... WHERE col = :var.col) [EDIT [KEY key$]] [TITLE t$] ...]
BROWSE.desc: Shows query results in a scrolling grid (arrows, PgUp/PgDn, Home/End, Left/Right for columns). Enter chooses a row: INTO gets it as a hash, like FOR row IN (SELECT ...). Esc gives an empty hash; check LASTKEY$. What the grid covered is put back when it ends. With EDIT, arrows move between cells, Enter or typing edits a cell, Ins adds a row, Del deletes one (after Y/N), and each change is saved at once (a table is edited by rowid; a query needs KEY "column"). A click on a heading, or F3, sorts by that column (again reverses it). Without EDIT, typing jumps to the next row whose sort column (or first column) starts with what was typed. FREEZE n keeps the first n columns in place when the others scroll; FORMAT shows columns with FORMAT$ masks, right-aligned; COLOR names a column holding each row's text colour (0-15), which is not shown. DETAIL adds a second grid below for the rows of the master's current row (INTO var holds it, so the DETAIL query uses :var.col); Enter or Tab on the master (F6 in an EDIT grid) or a click goes to the detail, Esc goes back, Esc on the master ends with INTO holding its current row, and lines added with Ins are linked to the master row. EXIT ON "PgUp,PgDn,F2" makes those keys end BROWSE so the program can handle them (LASTKEY$ says which). EDIT WHEN condition [MESSAGE text$] allows changes only while the condition holds (checked as the grid is shown, per master row for DETAIL).
examples: BROWSE (SELECT id, name FROM customers ORDER BY name) TITLE "Customers" INTO row
BROWSE (SELECT id, name, phone FROM customers) EDIT KEY "id"
BROWSE (SELECT name, city, balance, CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 12 END AS shade FROM customers) FREEZE 1 FORMAT balance "#,##0.00" COLOR "shade"
BROWSE (SELECT id, customer FROM orders) INTO o DETAIL (SELECT * FROM order_lines WHERE order_id = :o.id) EDIT KEY "line_id"

BROWSER.desc: Opens the specified URL in the default system web browser.

BUTTON$.desc: The label of the @ ... BUTTON that ended the last READ, or "" if READ ended another way (Esc, PgDn). A CANCEL button puts the fields' old values back but still returns its label.
examples:
@ 10, 5 BUTTON "Save"
@ 10, 15 BUTTON "Cancel" CANCEL
READ
IF BUTTON$ = "Save" THEN GOSUB save

CHAIN.desc: Transfers control to another script file and does not return. Variables are cleared unless PRESERVE is given. The arguments become its COMMAND$(1), COMMAND$(2), ...

CLOSE.desc: Closes a specific file number, or all open files if no number is given.

CLS.desc: Clears the screen in the current COLOR and moves the cursor to row 1, column 1. Pending GET fields are discarded.

COLOR.desc: Sets the text colours (0-15: 0 black, 1 blue, 2 green, 3 cyan, 4 red, 5 magenta, 6 brown, 7 white, 8-15 bright versions, 14 yellow). field_fg and field_bg colour GET fields, menu bars and the BROWSE bar (default black on white).

COPY.desc: Copies a file from one location to another.

CREATE.syntax: CREATE TABLE table_name (col1 TYPE, col2 TYPE...);
CREATE.desc: Creates a new table. Types: TEXT, INTEGER, REAL, BLOB.
examples: CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);

DATABASE.desc: Manages database connections. Type HELP DATABASE OPEN or HELP DATABASE ENGINE for details.

DATABASE ENGINE.desc: Switches the active database backend. Default is SQLITE.

DATABASE OPEN.desc: Opens a connection to a database file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist. Use ':memory:' for RAM-only.

DELETE.desc: Removes records from a table. Be careful without a WHERE clause!

DESCRIBE.desc: Prints the schema (columns and types) of a database table.

DIM.syntax: DIM var(size) OR DIM var AS HASH/ARRAY

DROP.desc: Permanently deletes a table and all its data.

EDIT.syntax:
EDIT RECORD (SELECT ... FROM table WHERE ...) [KEY key$] [AT top, left] [TITLE title$] [INTO var]
EDIT TEXT target [AT top, left, bottom, right] [TITLE title$]
EDIT.desc: EDIT TEXT is a boxed memo editor for a multi-line string (lines separated by CHR$(10)); Enter splits lines, Ctrl-Y deletes one, Ctrl-W or F10 saves, Esc cancels (asking first if changed). EDIT RECORD is a one-line entry form: one labelled field per column of the query's row. Enter on the last field or PgDn saves with an UPDATE of the changed columns; with no matching row the form starts blank and saves with an INSERT. KEY defaults to the table's primary key and can't be edited. A refused change shows the database's message and keeps the form open. INTO gets the saved record (empty after Esc).
examples: EDIT RECORD (SELECT * FROM contacts WHERE id = :id) TITLE "Contact"
EDIT RECORD (SELECT name, phone FROM customers WHERE code = :code$) KEY "code" INTO rec

EMAIL.desc: Sends an email using the configured provider (See: HELP SET EMAIL). Addresses and attachments are comma-separated lists. BODY is the plain-text part and HTMLBODY the HTML part; both may be given.
examples:
EMAIL TO "a@ex.com" CC "mgr@ex.com" SUBJECT "Report" HTMLBODY "

Attached.

" ATTACH "report.pdf"

ERROR.desc: Manually triggers an error with a custom code and message.
examples: IF x=0 THEN ERROR 1, "Div by Zero"

EXECUTE.desc: Runs one or more SQL statements held in a string, separated by semicolons. Query results are displayed. To run DDGBasic code from a string, use EVAL.
examples: EXECUTE "CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1);"

EXIT.syntax: EXIT FOR | EXIT WHILE | EXIT DO | EXIT FUNCTION | EXIT
EXIT.desc: EXIT FOR/WHILE/DO leaves the innermost loop of that kind. EXIT FUNCTION returns from a function. In the REPL, a bare EXIT leaves DDGBasic.

FETCH.syntax: FETCH "url" [POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE body_hash] [USING HEADERS req_h] [USING FILE field=path] INTO var$ | TO FILE "path" [HEADERS INTO resp_h]
FETCH.desc: Makes an HTTP request. Default method is GET. POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE send a hash as the request body (DELETE body optional). USING HEADERS attaches request headers from a hash. USING FILE does multipart file upload. INTO stores response text; TO FILE streams to disk. Optional HEADERS INTO captures response headers as a hash. Sets ERR to the HTTP status code (-1 network error, -2 file not found) and ERRMSG$ to the status and reason (e.g. 404 Not Found) or the error text. TO FILE writes the file only for a 2xx status.
examples: FETCH "https://api.com/data" INTO resp$ HEADERS INTO h
FETCH "https://api.com/upload" POST meta USING FILE "file"="local.pdf" INTO resp$

FILES.desc: Lists files matching a pattern. Can print to console or store in an array.
examples: FILES "data/*" INTO my_files RECURSIVE WITH FULLPATH

FILTER.desc: Returns a new array with elements that match the criteria. The criteria can be a substring (case-sensitive match against str(item)) or a bare user-defined function name (called with each item; truthy result includes the item). Optional include_flag = 0 inverts (returns NON-matches).

FOR.syntax: FOR var = start TO end [STEP step] ... NEXT
examples: FOR i = 1 TO 10: PRINT i: NEXT

FOR IN.syntax: FOR var IN (SELECT ...) | CSV "file" [OPTIONS "..."] | TEXT("file") | JSON("file") | JSONL("file") | FILES("pattern") ... NEXT
FOR IN.desc: Iterates over the rows of a query, the lines or records of a file, or the names of matching files.
examples: FOR row IN (SELECT id, name FROM users)

GOSUB.desc: Jumps to a subroutine at the specified label. RETURN command jumps back.

IF.syntax:
IF condition THEN ... [ELSE ...] 
OR
IF condition THEN
 ... 
[ELSEIF ...]
 ... 
END IF
examples: IF x > 10 THEN PRINT "Big" ELSE PRINT "Small"

IF x = 1 THEN
    PRINT "one"
ELSEIF x = 2 THEN
    PRINT "two"
ELSE
    PRINT "other"
END IF

INKEY$.desc: Returns the key pressed, or "" if none is waiting. INKEY$(0) waits for a key; INKEY$(n) waits up to n seconds. Keys come back as characters (Enter is CHR$(13), Esc CHR$(27), Tab CHR$(9)) or names: UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, HOME, END, PGUP, PGDN, INS, DEL, BTAB, F1-F12.
examples: IF INKEY$ = CHR$(27) THEN EXIT DO

INPUT.desc: Prompts the user for input and stores it in a variable.

INSERT.syntax: INSERT INTO table (col1, col2) VALUES (val1, val2);
INSERT.desc: Adds new records. You can use variables (e.g., :name$) as values.

KILL.desc: Deletes a file. A missing file sets ERR = 2 and continues, or calls the ON ERROR handler if one is active.

LASTKEY$.desc: The key that ended the last READ, MENU or BROWSE, or the last key INKEY$ returned.

LET.desc: Assigns a value to a variable. The LET keyword is optional.

LINE INPUT.desc: Reads a single line from an open file into a variable.

LOAD.desc: Imports data into a database table. Type HELP LOAD CSV for specifics.

LOAD CSV.syntax: LOAD CSV "file" CREATE TABLE name | INTO TABLE name [APPEND|TRUNCATE|UPSERT USING KEY col|IGNORE] [REJECTS INTO table] [OPTIONS "..."] [TRANSFORM col|ROW WITH fn]* [VALIDATE col|ROW WITH fn]* [USING SCHEMA "..."]
LOAD CSV.desc: Imports CSV data into a database table. TRANSFORM col WITH fn rewrites cells; TRANSFORM ROW WITH fn rewrites the whole row hash. VALIDATE col WITH fn / VALIDATE ROW WITH fn skip the row on falsy return. Clauses may be chained; column-level runs before row-level. REJECTS INTO table keeps the skipped rows, with _linenum, _reason and the source values.
examples: LOAD CSV "data.csv" INTO TABLE my_table TRUNCATE OPTIONS "header=true"
LOAD CSV "raw.csv" CREATE TABLE customers TRANSFORM phone WITH normalize_phone$
LOAD CSV "leads.csv" CREATE TABLE leads TRANSFORM name WITH PROPER$ VALIDATE email WITH is_valid_email
LOAD CSV "addrs.csv" CREATE TABLE a TRANSFORM ROW WITH fix_state_from_zip
LOAD CSV "rows.csv" CREATE TABLE r VALIDATE ROW WITH require_id_or_email
LOAD CSV "leads.csv" INTO TABLE leads REJECTS INTO leads_rejects VALIDATE email WITH is_valid_email

LOAD EXCEL.syntax: LOAD EXCEL "file.xlsx" CREATE TABLE name | INTO TABLE name [APPEND|TRUNCATE|UPSERT USING KEY col|IGNORE] [OPTIONS "sheetname=Sheet1"]
LOAD EXCEL.desc: Loads data from an Excel worksheet.

LOAD FIXED.syntax: LOAD FIXED "file" CREATE TABLE name | INTO TABLE name [APPEND|TRUNCATE|UPSERT USING KEY col|IGNORE] OPTIONS "fields=..."
LOAD FIXED.desc: Loads fixed-width files. Fields syntax: 'Name:Start-End' OR 'Name:Start+Length'.
examples: LOAD FIXED "dat.txt" INTO TABLE t OPTIONS "fields=ID:1-5,Name:6-20"
LOAD FIXED "dat.txt" INTO TABLE t OPTIONS "fields=ID:1+5,Name:6+15"

LOAD JSON.syntax: LOAD JSON "file" CREATE TABLE name | INTO TABLE name [APPEND|TRUNCATE|UPSERT USING KEY col|IGNORE] [OPTIONS "normalize=true"]
LOAD JSON.desc: Loads a JSON file. Use normalize=true to auto-relationalize nested data.

LOAD JSONL.syntax: LOAD JSONL "file" CREATE TABLE name | INTO TABLE name ... [OPTIONS "..."] [TRANSFORM col|ROW WITH fn]* [VALIDATE col|ROW WITH fn]*
LOAD JSONL.desc: Loads a JSON Lines file (one JSON object per line). Headers are inferred by sampling the first 'samplesize' lines (default 1000). TRANSFORM and VALIDATE clauses work identically to LOAD CSV.
examples: LOAD JSONL "leads.jsonl" CREATE TABLE leads TRANSFORM phone WITH normalize_phone$ VALIDATE email WITH is_valid_email

LOAD PARQUET.syntax: LOAD PARQUET "file" CREATE TABLE name | INTO TABLE name ... [OPTIONS "..."] [TRANSFORM col|ROW WITH fn]* [VALIDATE col|ROW WITH fn]*
LOAD PARQUET.desc: Loads an Apache Parquet file. Streams via row groups; complex column types (structs, lists) are serialized to JSON strings. TRANSFORM and VALIDATE clauses work identically to LOAD CSV.
examples: LOAD PARQUET "raw.parquet" CREATE TABLE clean VALIDATE ROW WITH is_well_formed

LOCATE.desc: Moves the cursor; the next PRINT starts there. Rows and columns count from 1 at the top left.

MAKE FORM.syntax: MAKE FORM table$ TO file$ [KEY column$] [TITLE title$]
MAKE FORM.desc: Writes a complete data-entry program for a table, to edit as you like: a menu bar (Browse, Add, Edit, Delete), an editable grid, and an entry form with a field for each column chosen from its type (text widths, number masks, @D dates, CHECKBOX for BOOLEAN, a drop-down LIST for a foreign key, required NOT NULL fields), hints, F1 help, and ALERTs for changes the database refuses. The program opens the current database file, so open one first. KEY names the column that identifies a row (default: the primary key, or SQLite's rowid). The file must not exist yet.

MAP.desc: Returns a new array with each element passed through a user-defined transform function. The function is called once per element with that element as its single argument.

MENU.syntax: choice = MENU(row, col, item1$, item2$, ... | items_array)
MENU.desc: Shows a boxed light-bar menu. Arrows move, Enter chooses, the first letter of an item chooses it directly. Returns the item number from 1, or 0 for Esc. What the menu covered is put back when it returns. A menu longer than the screen scrolls (PgUp/PgDn move a page).

MENUBAR$.desc: Draws a menu bar (row 1 unless given) with a pull-down menu under each title. Items are separated by |; '-' is a separator; a title without items is chosen directly. Left/Right move between menus, Enter/Down open and choose, a first letter chooses. Returns "Title.Item" (or "Title"), or "" for Esc. The bar stays drawn; the pull-downs are removed.
examples:
choice$ = MENUBAR$("File:Open|Save|-|Quit", "Customers:Browse|Add", "Help:About")
IF choice$ = "File.Quit" THEN END

MOUSEROW.desc: The row and column (from 1) of the last mouse click or wheel turn. INKEY$ returns CLICK, RCLICK, MCLICK, WHEELUP or WHEELDOWN for them. The screen statements (READ, MENU, ALERT, MENUBAR$, BROWSE, EDIT TEXT, VIEW) take clicks themselves. SET MOUSE OFF turns the mouse off.
examples:
k$ = INKEY$(0)
IF k$ = "CLICK" THEN @ MOUSEROW, MOUSECOL SAY "*"

ON ERROR.desc: Defines an error handler. If an error occurs, execution jumps to the label.

ON KEY.syntax: ON KEY key$ CALL function | ON KEY key$ OFF
ON KEY.desc: Makes a key run a FUNCTION (no arguments) whenever the program waits for a key: READ, BROWSE, MENU, MENUBAR$, ALERT, EDIT TEXT, VIEW, INKEY$. The screen is put back afterwards. Key names: F1-F12, CTRL-A..CTRL-Z, ALT-A..ALT-Z, UP, DOWN, DEL, ENTER, ESC, TAB, SPACE, or one character.

OPEN.desc: Opens a file for reading or writing using a file number.

PARSEJSON.desc: Parses a JSON string and returns a structured object (Hash/List) that can be accessed by key or index.

POP.desc: Removes the last element from an array. Optionally saves it to a variable.

PRINT.desc: Outputs text or values to the console. Use ; to suppress newline.

PRINT USING.desc: Formats numeric output using a mask string. Supports # for digits, comma separators, and $$ for currency.

PROGRESS.syntax: PROGRESS done, total [TITLE t$] | PROGRESS OFF
PROGRESS.desc: Shows a centred box with a progress bar and a percentage; later calls update it in place (drawing only what changed). PROGRESS OFF removes it and puts back what it covered.
examples:
FOR i = 1 TO n
    PROGRESS i, n TITLE "Copying"
NEXT i
PROGRESS OFF

PUSH.desc: Adds an element to the end of an array.

QR.syntax:
QR text$ [AT row, col] [TO file$]
QR$(text$)
QR.desc: Makes a QR code of the text (a web address, an order number, a Wi-Fi login, a contact card). AT draws it on the screen at row, col, as dark squares on white so phones can scan it; a web address takes about 33 columns and 17 rows. TO saves it as a .png or .svg image to print. With neither, it is printed like PRINT. QR$(text$) returns it as lines of text made of █ ▀ ▄ characters.

READ.desc: Edits the GET fields in order. Tab/Enter/Down go to the next field, Shift-Tab/Up to the previous one, PgDn or Ctrl-W finish, Ctrl-Y clears a field, Ins toggles insert mode. Enter on the last field finishes. Esc puts back the values the variables had and ends READ; check LASTKEY$ = CHR$(27). With SET AUTOADVANCE ON (or Clipper's SET CONFIRM OFF), filling a field's last position moves to the next field.
examples:
READ
IF LASTKEY$ = CHR$(27) THEN GOTO cancelled

READ FILE.desc: Reads the entire contents of a file into a single string variable.

REDUCE.desc: Folds an array into a single value. The accumulator function takes (acc, item) and returns the new accumulator. If initial is omitted, the first element is used as the initial accumulator and iteration begins at the second element (errors if array is empty).
examples: maxval = REDUCE(nums, max_of)            ` no initial -- uses nums(0)

REPORT.syntax: REPORT (SELECT ...) [TITLE title$] [GROUP BY col, ...] [TOTAL col, ...] [FORMAT col mask$, ...] [PAGE lines] [TO FILE path$ | TO VIEW | INTO var$]
REPORT.desc: Prints a query as a report: a title line with the date, column headings, a heading and a subtotal footer for each group (the query must be sorted by the GROUP BY columns), grand totals, and pages with PAGE. FORMAT uses FORMAT$ masks. The report goes to the screen unless TO FILE, TO VIEW or INTO is given.
examples: REPORT (SELECT region, customer, amount FROM sales ORDER BY region) GROUP BY region TOTAL amount FORMAT amount "#,##0.00"
REPORT (SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY id) TITLE "Orders" PAGE 60 TO FILE "orders.txt"

RESTSCREEN.desc: Puts back the screen area saved by SAVESCREEN, in the same place, and returns the cursor to where it was.

RESUME.desc: Returns from an error handler. RESUME NEXT continues with the statement after the one that failed; RESUME label continues at the label.

REVERSE.desc: Reverses the order of elements in an array in place.

RUN.desc: Runs another script file as a child program; the arguments become its COMMAND$(1), COMMAND$(2), ... When it finishes (or reaches END), control returns to the calling program and its variables are restored (unlike CHAIN).

SAVESCREEN.syntax: saved$ = SAVESCREEN() | SAVESCREEN(top, left, bottom, right)
SAVESCREEN.desc: Copies the screen, or an area of it, with its colours and the cursor position into a string for RESTSCREEN. It covers what screen statements, PRINT and INPUT drew; query tables and SHELL output are not included.
examples:
saved$ = SAVESCREEN(8, 20, 14, 60)
BOX 8, 20, 14, 60, "Warning" DOUBLE
k$ = INKEY$(0)
RESTSCREEN saved$

SELECT.syntax: SELECT column1, column2 FROM table_name [WHERE condition];
SELECT.desc: Retrieves data from a database. Must end with a semicolon.
examples: SELECT id, name FROM customers WHERE id > 100 ORDER BY name;

SET.desc: Configures system behavior. Type HELP SET OUTPUT or HELP SET EMAIL for details.

SET EMAIL.syntax: SET EMAIL PROVIDER "SMTP" HOST "..." PORT n USER "..." PASSWORD "..." SENDER "..."
SET EMAIL.desc: Configures the email provider (SMTP, SENDGRID, MAILGUN).
examples: SET EMAIL PROVIDER "SMTP" HOST "smtp.mail.com" PORT 587 USER "me" PASSWORD "pass" SENDER "me@mail.com"

SET HASH_KEYS.desc: Controls case sensitivity for hash keys (Dictionaries). Default is PRESERVE_CASE.

SET NULL_HANDLING.desc: Controls how LOAD stores empty (or all-space) fields: NULL (the default) or EMPTY to keep ''. FOR "col" or FOR "table.col" sets one column.

SET OUTPUT.desc: Redirects query output. Formats: TEXT (or TABLE), CSV, JSON, JSONL, XML, HTML, FIXED, PLAIN, SQL, EXCEL, PARQUET. FILE replaces the file on each query; FILE ... APPEND adds each result (one CSV header). OFF still runs queries but shows no rows.
examples: SET OUTPUT CONSOLE FORMAT TABLE OPTIONS "box_style=ASCII"
SET OUTPUT FILE "dump.sql" FORMAT SQL INSERT
SET OUTPUT FILE "dump.sql" FORMAT SQL OPTIONS "mode=update, target_tablename=users"

SET SQL_FATAL_ERRORS.desc: If ON (default), SQL errors stop the program. If OFF, they set ERR variable.

SET STYLE.desc: Sets the look of text screens. modern (the default) draws the 16 colour numbers of COLOR in softer tones (1, the classic blue background, is a charcoal; 3, the field colour, a light steel blue; the bright colours are muted), boxes with thin rounded corners, and flat buttons. classic is the 1990s look: the terminal's own 16 colours, double-line boxes and [ buttons ]. Use CLS afterwards to repaint the screen.

SET THEME.desc: Sets the four screen colours of COLOR at once from a named theme: default (white on black), classic (white on blue, the 1990s business look), norton (cyan on blue), green (a green screen), amber (an amber monitor), paper (black on white) or mono. Use CLS afterwards to repaint the screen in it.

SHELL.desc: Run a command in the underlying operating system shell.

SHIFT.desc: Removes the first element from an array. Optionally saves it.

SHOW CREATE TABLE.desc: Displays the CREATE TABLE statement for one table, or for all tables.

SHOW INDEXES.desc: Lists the indexes, primary keys and unique constraints of one table, or of all tables.

SHOW TABLES.desc: Lists all tables found in the currently open database.

SHOW VARIABLES.desc: Debug command. Prints the names, types, and values of all current variables.

SORT.desc: Sorts an array. Use ON to sort an array of hashes by a string key. Use WITH to sort by a function (UDF or built-in) that returns each element's sort key.

SPLICE.syntax: SPLICE array, start, count [, val1, val2...]
SPLICE.desc: Removes 'count' items starting at 'start'. Optionally inserts new items there.

SQL.desc:
Executes standard SQL statements directly.
Syntax depends on current database engine.
SQL statements MUST end with a semi-colon.

TIMER.desc: The number of seconds since midnight, with fractions of a second, as in classic BASIC. Take it before and after some work to time it.

TROFF.desc: Turns TRace OFF. Stops printing executed lines.

TRON.desc: Turns TRace ON. The interpreter will print each line of code before executing it.

UNSHIFT.desc: Adds an element to the beginning of an array.

UNZIP.desc: Extracts files from a ZIP archive. Defaults to current directory if TO is omitted.

UPDATE.syntax: UPDATE table_name SET col1 = val1 WHERE condition;
UPDATE.desc: Modifies existing records. Must end with a semicolon.
examples: UPDATE users SET status = 'Active' WHERE id = 1;

UPGRADE.desc: Transforms raw files to match a Master Schema. Type HELP UPGRADE CSV for details.

UPGRADE CSV.desc: Standardizes CSV headers, order, and values based on a schema generated by ANALYZE CSV.

UPGRADE JSON.desc: Rewrites a JSON file to strictly match a schema (from ANALYZE JSON). Fills missing keys.

UPGRADE XML.desc: Rewrites XML files to enforce a consistent tag structure defined by ANALYZE XML.

VIEW.syntax: VIEW FILE path$ | VIEW (SELECT ...) | VIEW text$  [AT top, left, bottom, right] [TITLE title$]
VIEW.desc: Shows a file, a query result (as a text table) or a string in a read-only, scrolling box. Arrows, PgUp/PgDn, Home/End and Left/Right move; / (or Ctrl-F) searches, ignoring case; n or F3 finds the next match; Esc or q closes. The screen is put back afterwards.
examples: VIEW (SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY id) TITLE "Orders"

WHILE.desc: Repeats a block of statements as long as the condition is true.

WRITE.desc: Writes data to a file (or console) in CSV format. Strings are quoted, numbers are not.
